clue.text: Cross about mongrel showing up, if one must get cross

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: in a down clue a word showing up is read from bottom to top, so it runs backwards

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A grumpy remark that someone must lose their temper when a scruffy dog turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing up' turns CUR to RUC; 'must get' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A crucifix is a cross bearing the figure of Christ, so the noun is an exact synonym.

clue.text: Boss taking the cake, as man on Muscle Beach?

parts.note: a boss is a stud, a raised knob as on a shield
a muffin is a small cake

explanation.surface: A bodybuilder on a famous California beach wins first prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking the cake' looks like an idiom for winning; here it just adds the cake. Muscle Beach is a bodybuilding spot in California, so its men are hunks.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a sexy, muscular young man, the kind seen flexing on Muscle Beach, hence the question mark.

clue.text: See 2
Important to retain office, standing under new US president

indicators.note: to retain is to hold on to, so the outer word keeps the other pieces inside it

parts.note: key means important, as in a key figure

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece under another is written after it
in a down clue a standing word is set upright, read bottom to top, so it runs backwards

parts.note: a den is a private study or office

explanation.surface: A politician must keep his job while standing below a newly elected American president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' is the usual down-clue reversal signal; 'to retain' wraps the outer word round the rest, and 'under' sets the turned office after the N.
explanation.definitionFit: John F Kennedy was the 35th President of the United States, so the name is an example of the category.

clue.text: Sweatier pants, so to speak

indicators.note: pants as a verb means gasps, but as slang 'pants' means rubbish, so the letters are messed up

explanation.surface: Someone joking that sweatier underwear is a figure of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' (British slang for rubbish) signals rearranging SWEATIER; it looks like underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms flagging that words are used loosely or figuratively.

clue.text: Primarily baker can't cook, perhaps, where accidents waiting to happen?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: someone who lacks pots might be unable to cook, a playful reading

explanation.surface: A baker unable to cook might be a hazard waiting to happen.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'can't cook, perhaps' is reinterpreted as LACKS POTS; 'perhaps' flags that this is one possible reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Black spots are stretches of road where accidents repeatedly occur, a fixed idiom for danger zones.

clue.text: Inventive mind is working under Rusbridger, say

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece below another comes after it

parts.note: Alan Rusbridger was editor of the Guardian, and ED is short for editor
taken as written
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: A creative thinker employed beneath the Guardian's editor.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Rusbridger edited the Guardian when this puzzle appeared; 'say' marks him as an example of an editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was a prolific inventor, so his name stands for a great inventive mind.

clue.text: Supporting front of tarpaulin, gets filthy stick out

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is taken

parts.note: rude can mean filthy, as in a rude joke

explanation.surface: A dirty tarpaulin sheet poking out at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To protrude is to project beyond a surface, the same meaning as the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Girl looking at something saucy

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally
addressing a problem means looking at it, turning attention to it

explanation.surface: A girl eyeing up something cheeky or risqué.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saucy' suggests cheekiness, but here it means literally like a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad dressing is a sauce poured on salad, so it is literally something saucy.

clue.text: Move quickly, bringing first of contraband into the south of France

indicators.note: into says one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: sud is the French word for south

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Smuggling goods into the Riviera at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the south of France' looks like a region, but means the French word for south, SUD.
explanation.definitionFit: To scud is to race along swiftly, like clouds driven by wind.

clue.text: Within such, the madness of maniac fits?

definitions.text: Within such, the madness of maniac fits?

indicators.note: madness suggests disorder, so the letters of the following words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A remark that inside extreme zeal, a lunatic's fits of madness lie.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'maniac' as a noun and 'fits' as a verb: the maniac suits fanaticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Fanaticism is excessive zeal, exactly the frenzy a maniac shows, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Dog's coat

definitions.meaning: a long-haired hunting hound breed from central Asia; 's is read as 'is'
a sheepskin coat with embroidery, fashionable in the 1960s

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a long-haired hound breed and a sheepskin coat, two separate senses.

clue.text: Purpose in very warm weather to ensure no squatting indoors?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: hot rain would be very warm weather
use means purpose, as in what is the use

explanation.surface: Tropical rainstorms serving to keep squatters out of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squatting' suggests illegal occupation, but means a pet crouching to relieve itself indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Training a pet to relieve itself outside means it will not crouch and soil the floor indoors.

clue.text: See 9
Old joke starts to get embarrassing, so delete

parts.note: ex means former, old
a pun is a joke on words

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters, taken from each of the next two words

explanation.surface: Removing a stale joke before it becomes embarrassing.
explanation.definitionFit: To expunge is to erase or remove completely, a synonym for delete.

clue.text: Giant character decapitated ambitious type

parts.note: Gog is a legendary giant, as in Gog and Magog

indicators.note: decapitated means the head is cut off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a letter is a written character

explanation.surface: A fearsome giant beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: Gog and Magog are giants of British legend, with statues at London's Guildhall.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-getter is an energetic, ambitious person, the same type.

clue.text: Spray a painful back with cold contents

indicators.note: back says the word goes the other way round

parts.note: sore means painful

indicators.note: contents are what lies inside, so the letters between the first and last

explanation.surface: A spray for a sore back containing a cooling agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SORE to EROS; 'contents' of COLD are OL.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol is a pressurised can that sprays its contents as a fine mist.

clue.text: Old poem, like "Far Away"?

parts.note: verse is poetry, or a poem
as means like, in the manner of

explanation.surface: An old poem with a title like Far Away.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks pretend Far Away is a poem's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Overseas means in a distant foreign land, so it is a synonym for a distant location.

clue.text: Turkish city drifting to China

indicators.note: drifting means wandering out of position, so the letters move around

explanation.surface: A Turkish city floating towards China.
explanation.walkthrough: Antioch, now Antakya, is in southern Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch is the ancient name of the city of Antakya in southern Turkey.

clue.text: Right to enter claim with name which provokes a reaction

indicators.note: to enter is to go into, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to allege is to claim

explanation.surface: A legal claim of rights with someone's name provoking a response.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergen is a substance that triggers an allergic response in the body.

clue.text: Sumptuous, like a throne room?

parts.note: the throne is a jokey word for the toilet, so its room is a lav (lavatory)
the suffix -ish means like, somewhat

explanation.surface: A grand palace room where the monarch sits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throne room' suggests royalty, but the throne is a toilet seat, so it is the LAV, British slang for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavish means luxurious and extravagant, a synonym for sumptuous.

clue.text: Imagine holding pose, showing box

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: bet can mean an opinion or guess, as in my bet is
to pose a question is to ask

explanation.surface: Picturing someone striking a pose while showing a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A basket is a woven container, a kind of box or receptacle.

clue.text: In which old prostitutes going about upside-down clinches

indicators.note: in a down clue upside-down means read from the bottom upwards, so backwards
clinches means holds tight, so the phrase holds the letters within it

explanation.surface: A tangled picture of people going around embracing upside-down.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters OINGAB sit inside 'going about'; 'upside-down' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagnio is an old word for a brothel, where prostitutes worked.

clue.text: What the very thin girl eats — to get fat?

definitions.text: What the very thin girl eats — to get fat?

indicators.note: eats means takes inside, so the answer is swallowed by the phrase

explanation.surface: Asking what a skinny girl should eat to put on weight.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'thE VERY THIN Girl'; the whole clue is also the definition: eating all of it would fatten anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating all food, without exception, would make a thin girl fat.

clue.text: Patient's chest

definitions.meaning: a doctor's patient; 's is read as 'is'
a chest is a box or packing container

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a medical patient and a box or packing trunk.

clue.text: Tilt item with hands, dropping left

indicators.note: dropping means letting go of a letter

parts.note: a clock has hands

explanation.surface: Tipping an object held in someone's hands and letting go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'item with hands' is a clock face, not something held.
explanation.definitionFit: To cock is to tilt at an angle, as in cocking the head.

clue.text: While hidden, shoot bird

definitions.meaning: to fire at someone from a concealed position
a wading bird with a long bill

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to fire from cover, as a sniper does, and a long-billed wading bird.

clue.text: Note on flier, inconsequential communication

parts.note: a chit is a short note
a chat is a small songbird, so a flier

explanation.surface: A note attached to a bird, carrying trivial messages.
explanation.definitionFit: Chit-chat is light small talk, trivial conversation.
